newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates rise on short crop fear.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates rise on short crop fear.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Sunday amid speculation about the size of the 1996/97 (July-June) crop, dealers said.

They said spinners covered their positions ahead of an announcement estimating the crop size by a standing committee that includes farmers, ginners, spinners and officials. The committee was expected to announce its estimate later on Sunday.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,250 rupees ($55.94) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
